name: Lishanid Noshan
catalog_quote: In citation forms stress falls on the last syllable of nouns. In context stress is always retracted to the penult. If the penult is a short epenthetic, stress is antepenultimate. In verbs, the last vowel of the root is usually stressed (Khan 19 :70).

sources.quote: Khan 1999:70 (sec. 5.1 Nominals): "In most nominals the stress falls on either the final or penultimate syllable. Occasionally it falls on the antepenult. The end of the word should be regarded as the basic position. Placement of stress on earlier syllables will be referred to as retraction from the basic position. This is reflected by the fact that the citation forms of nominals are stressed on the final syllable. (i) Stress in basic position: hasta 'work' (Y:1), qalla 'citadel' (Y:24) ..."; p.

sources.quote: "In general, word stress falls on the final syllable of nominal and verbal stems in Mlahsô ... and the eastern Jewish NENA dialects, i.e., those of Arbel, Rustaqa/Ruwanduz, Sulemaniyya and Halabja, and Koy Sanjaq in eastern Iraqi Kurdistan (Khan 1999a: 70-74, 2004: 61ff. Mutzafi 2004b: 55f.) ... In the remaining MA dialects, stress is penultimate"; fn. 22: "With variable retraction to the preceding syllable, especially in certain categories such as vocatives; for examples, see Khan 2002b."
